name: What are the differences between zoning for a tiny home on a foundation versus one on wheels?

mainEntity.name: What are the differences between zoning for a tiny home on a foundation versus one on wheels?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zoning for a tiny home on a foundation treats it as a permanent structure, often an ADU, subject to standard building codes, property taxes, and long-term residency rules. A tiny home on wheels, however, is typically classified as a recreational vehicle (RV) or mobile home. This means it may be subject to different regulations regarding parking, occupancy duration, and utility hookups, and might not be allowed as a permanent dwelling in many residential zones. The distinction is critical for legal placement.
acceptedAnswer.description: Foundation tiny homes are permanent structures subject to building codes, while tiny homes on wheels are often classified as RVs with different rules for parking and occupancy.
